# Fractures
Heavy hits can break bones. A broken bone hurts, and moving on one that isn't supported can make it worse.
## Severity From least to most serious: - [bold]Hairline[/bold]: a crack. - [bold]Simple[/bold]: a clean break. - [bold]Compound[/bold]: the bone has broken through. It also bleeds internally. - [bold]Shattered[/bold]: the bone is in pieces. It bleeds internally even faster.
Examining a patient shows fractures, and a health analyzer shows them to anyone with basic medical training. With more training it shows the exact severity.
## Splints - A splint stabilizes a broken limb, so moving on it stops making it worse. It works on hairline and simple fractures. - [bold]A splint doesn't heal the bone.[/bold] It only holds things together until the patient can get a cast or surgery. - Each splint has 4 uses and takes 3 seconds to apply.
## Casts - A cast immobilizes a hairline or simple fracture and heals it completely over 5 minutes. - Each cast has 4 uses and takes 6 seconds to apply. - When the bone has healed, the patient is told the cast is ready to come off. Remove it with the [bold]Remove cast[/bold] option. - If the bone breaks again while it's in a cast, the cast cracks apart. - [bold]OsteoCalc[/bold] speeds up bone healing by half again while it's in the patient's system.
## Surgery Compound and shattered fractures can't be fixed with a cast; they need surgery. Surgery can fix any fracture, including hairline and simple ones. - [bold]Set Simple Fracture[/bold] (hairline or simple): open the incision, realign the bone with a bone setter, apply bone gel, then close up. - [bold]Set Compound Fracture[/bold]: open the incision, realign the bone with a bone setter, apply bone gel, then close up. - [bold]Set Shattered Fracture[/bold]: open the incision, realign the bone with a bone setter, apply bone gel, insert a bone graft, set it with the bone setter again, then close up. - Fractures in the chest or skull are reached by opening the bone cavity first.
See [textlink="Surgery" link="CMUGuideMedicalSurgery"] for how to operate.
## After Surgery - [color=red]Put a cast on within 5 minutes of setting a bone.[/color] If you don't, there's a 30% chance it sets wrong, leaving the patient with a simple fracture again. - A cast on a freshly set bone finishes healing it in 5 minutes. A cast also fixes a bone that has set wrong.
